# Project description

What one ECU software uses of its board: system clock, used buses and channels with bit rates, PWM frequency and dead time, memory partitioning, bootloader and diagnostic addresses, interrupt ranks, loads at ADC channels, safety pins and module parameters. The project is the one input a build starts from.

Configuration level: **Project**. File: `projects/<project>/project.yaml`. Schema: `Project` in [`tools/nxconfig/model.py`](../../tools/nxconfig/model.py).

221 fields in 46 objects. 0 fields have no description in the schema and 0 numeric fields have no unit; they are marked _missing in schema_ and _missing_. How to read the tables: [reference overview](README.md).

### `project`

Identification of the project and the files it is built from.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project.name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Project name; by convention the same as the folder `projects/<project>`. |
| `project.board` | string |  | yes |  |  | Board folder or its `board.yaml`, relative to `project.yaml`. |
| `project.rte` | string |  | no | `null` |  | ECU description (`rte.yaml`) for tools/rtegen, relative to `project.yaml`. Required: the build runs rtegen at every configure, and nxconfig refuses a project that is built without it (TOOL-114). An ECU without software components still has one: one task, `components: []`. |
| `project.diag` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Diagnostic description (`diag.yaml`): data identifiers, routines, sessions, security levels and DTCs of this ECU software, relative to `project.yaml`. Left out: the project describes no diagnostic jobs and no fault memory. |
| `project.description` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Short description of the project for the reader. |
| `project.integrity` | string |  | no | `null` | `qm`, `asil_a`, `asil_b`, `asil_c`, `asil_d` | Highest safety integrity the ECU software of this project carries (ASIL of its safety requirements). `qm`: no safety requirement; the checks that are stricter for ASIL projects then only warn (e.g. a BSW task stack below its default without a proof note, bsw_tasks.&lt;task>.evidence). Not `qm` while an NvM block has an ASIL integrity. Left out: treated as an ASIL project - the safety part of neXtBSW (safety task, safe supervisor) is in every image. |

<a id="f-memory-application"></a>

### `memory.application`

RAM of the application. The no-init area (hard fault dump, boot request) ends at the end of the last region.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `memory.application.ram` | list of string |  | yes |  | at least 1 item; item: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | RAM regions of the derivative the application uses, in address order and contiguous. |
| `memory.application.noinit_size` | integer | byte | yes |  | > 0 | Size of the no-init area at the end of the last RAM region: it survives a reset and holds the hard fault dump and the boot request. |
| `memory.application.ramfunctions_size` | integer | byte | no | `null` | > 0 | RAM for flash routines that run from RAM (`.launchFromRAM`), at the start of the RAM. Small derivatives (e.g. 14 KB SRAM) need less than the template default. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x1000). |
| `memory.application.hot_ram_size` | integer | byte | no | `null` | > 0 | Hot part at the start of the RAM: RAM functions plus hot data and bss. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x2000 with a single RAM region, otherwise the whole first region). |
| `memory.application.isr_stack_size` | integer | byte | no | `null` | > 0 | Interrupt stack (main stack: start-up up to the scheduler plus every interrupt level nested). Multiple of 8. Size it with the worst case of tools/stackuse for the image plus a reserve. Left out: the default of the linker template (0x1000). |
| `memory.application.isr_stack_guard_size` | integer | byte | no | `null` | > 0 | Guard directly below the interrupt stack that the core may read but not write (MPU): an overflow ends in the hard fault reaction instead of overwriting data. Multiple of 32 (MPU granularity); it must hold the largest frame on the interrupt stack plus the larger of that frame and an exception frame (tools/stackuse checks it). Left out: the default of the linker template (0x400). |
| `memory.application.isr_stack_evidence` | [object](#f-memory-application-isr_stack_evidence) |  | no | `null` |  | Proof note of the interrupt stack: `used_bytes` is the worst case on the main stack (start-up plus every interrupt level nested, tools/stackuse --strict for this image) or the high-water mark at the board (inject mspuse). Required for `isr_stack_size` below the default of the linker template in an ASIL project (project.integrity not `qm`), otherwise a warning. The interrupt stack must hold `used_bytes`. Left out: no proof noted. |
| `memory.application.isr_stack_guard_evidence` | [object](#f-memory-application-isr_stack_guard_evidence) |  | no | `null` |  | Proof note of the guard: `used_bytes` is the guard tools/stackuse --strict requires for this image (largest frame on the interrupt stack plus the larger of that frame and an exception frame); only `method: stackuse`, a measurement cannot show it. Required for `isr_stack_guard_size` below the default in an ASIL project, otherwise a warning. The guard must hold `used_bytes`. Left out: no proof noted. |

<a id="f-memory-calibration"></a>

### `memory.calibration`

Calibration segment: the values of all calibration parameters (rte::PARAMETERS) in a flash area of their own, behind a `CALV` header (magic, format, layout identifier, length, CRC-32). The application checks the header at start-up and reacts as `on_invalid` says. tools/nxconfig/memory.py places it: in the code flash of `memory.flash` directly behind the first sector of the application (the vector table stays where the bootloader jumps to), so the download of the application does not grow over the whole flash.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `memory.calibration.region` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Flash region of the derivative the segment lies in: the code flash of `memory.flash`, or a data flash region (kind `data_flash`). A data flash can only be written separately, which the bootloader learns with BL-31 (NVM-12); until then it is refused with that reason. |
| `memory.calibration.size` | integer | byte | yes |  | > 0 | Size of the segment, whole sectors of the region: 32 bytes of header plus the values of all calibration parameters (the linker checks that they fit). |
| `memory.calibration.on_invalid` | string |  | no | `"refuse"` | `refuse`, `defaults`, `warn` | Reaction at start-up when the header, the layout identifier or the CRC of the segment does not fit the application. `refuse`: the application functions (RTE runnables) do not start, the ECU stays reachable over UDS for a new download; required as soon as one parameter is safety relevant (`safety` of swc.yaml other than qm). `defaults`: the values built into the application image, development profile only. `warn`: the values of the segment as they are. Each reaction other than a valid segment is logged and reported to the fault memory (BSW event `calibration.segment`). |
| `memory.calibration.profile` | string |  | no | `"development"` | `development`, `production` | `development`: the values are copied into a RAM working page at start-up, XCP calibrates there, the flash segment is the reference page. `production`: the values are read directly from the flash segment, there is no RAM copy and no write path; the project must not have an `xcp` section. |

<a id="f-nvm-partition"></a>

### `nvm.partition`

Split of the emulated EEPROM, in bytes; the generator derives the codes of the partition command from the derivative (`eeprom_emulation`).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nvm.partition.eeprom_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes of emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx: FlexRAM used as EEPROM). One of the sizes of the derivative. |
| `nvm.partition.data_flash_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Bytes of the partitionable flash that stay data flash; the rest backs up the emulated EEPROM. |
| `nvm.partition.partition_code` | integer | none | no | `null` | 0 to 15 | Code of the split in the partition command (s32k1xx: DEPART). Only needed where the derivative has several codes for the same split; it must be one of them. |
| `nvm.partition.load_on_reset` | boolean |  | no | `true` |  | `true`: the chip loads the emulated EEPROM during every reset (s32k1xx: PGMPART FCCOB3 = 0, IFR EEERST = 1 - opposite encodings). `false`: every start would need a flash command (SETRAM), which the start-up never launches; the NvM would run on its defaults. |
| `nvm.partition.key_slots` | integer | none | no | `null` | ≥ 0 | NVM-11: key slots of the security module to reserve in the emulated EEPROM (s32k1xx CSEc: 0, 5, 10 or 20; FCCOB1). One of the key space sizes of the derivative; the bytes come off the usable EEPROM. Left out on a derivative with a key space: the partition command refuses to write - the space is fixed with the partition and cannot be added later. |
| `nvm.partition.key_verify_only` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | NVM-11: security flag extension (s32k1xx: SFE, FCCOB2): lets a key be marked verify-only. Not offered yet: the partition command writes it off. |

<a id="f-nvm-blocks-key"></a>

### `nvm.blocks.<key>`

Definition of one NvM block (NVM-18: data type, scalar or vector, integrity), its place and write policy.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.type` | string |  | no | `null` | `boolean`, `uint8`, `sint8`, `uint16`, `sint16`, `uint32`, `sint32`, `float32`, `float64` | NVM-18: platform type of the block's value (of one element of a vector). The ports connected to `nvm.<Block>` must have this type. Left out: the type comes from the writing port (before NVM-18; the generator warns and proposes the definition). Not for the blocks of the fault memory (DemEvents, DemEntries), whose layout comes from diag.yaml. |
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.length` | integer | none | no | `null` | > 0 | NVM-18: 1 = scalar, more = vector (array) of that many elements of `type`. Left out: 1. Only with `type`. |
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.integrity` | string |  | no | `null` | `qm`, `asil_a`, `asil_b`, `asil_c`, `asil_d` | NVM-18: `qm`: one stored value with CRC-16 (as before). `asil_a` .. `asil_d`: two copies, each with CRC-32 and write counter; a defective copy is repaired from the other and reported to the fault memory, with both defective the block starts from its default and the application reads the quality 'unsecured' (`nvm.qlf.<Block>`). All ASIL levels use the same mechanism. Left out: `qm`. |
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.address` | integer | byte | no | `null` | ≥ 0 | Offset of the block's first slot in the emulated EEPROM, a multiple of 4. Left out: laid out after the fixed blocks, in name order. |
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.write` | string |  | no | `null` | `shutdown`, `change` | `shutdown`: written at the run-down and on request. `change`: also cyclically after a change, at most once per `min_interval_ms`. Left out: the default of the block (blocks of components `shutdown`, blocks of the fault memory from diag.yaml). |
| `nvm.blocks.<key>.min_interval_ms` | integer | ms | no | `null` | > 0 | Only with `write: change`: shortest time between two writes of the block. |

<a id="f-nvm-data_flash"></a>

### `nvm.data_flash`

NVM-12: what the data flash holds. tools/nxconfig checks it against the part the partition leaves as data flash (`nvm.partition.data_flash_bytes`, or the whole data flash region of a derivative without partition) and lays it out; tools/bswgen generates the table (nvm/nvmDataFlash.h).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nvm.data_flash.areas` | map of string to [object](#f-nvm-data_flash-areas-key) |  | yes |  | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Areas of the data flash; key: area name (C identifier, the name in the generated table). |

<a id="f-nvm-data_flash-areas-key"></a>

### `nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>`

NVM-12: one area of the data flash - whole sectors the application reads like memory and erases and programs at run time (libs/bsw/nvmDataFlash, dataflash::AreaService).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.size` | integer | byte | yes |  | > 0 | Size of the area, whole sectors of the data flash region of the derivative (they are erased on their own). |
| `nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.purpose` | string |  | yes |  | `calibration`, `data` | `calibration`: calibration data changed in the device (maps, data sets). `data`: other data of the application. Not for logs or images (the user's purpose 2026-09-28: calibration data). |
| `nvm.data_flash.areas.<key>.offset` | integer | byte | no | `null` | ≥ 0 | Offset of the area in the data flash, a multiple of the sector size. Left out: laid out after the fixed areas, in name order. |

<a id="f-security"></a>

### `security`

Keys of the hardware security module the project loads (s32k1xx: CSEc; SHE key names). The key space itself is reserved by `nvm.partition.key_slots`.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `security.stage` | string |  | no | `"development"` | `development`, `production` | `development`: development boards; every board of the project gets the same MASTER_ECU_KEY from the key store of the workstation, so the debug authentication can bring any of them back to the factory state. `production`: per device keys - not offered yet, refused. |
| `security.master_ecu_key` | string |  | no | `null` | 1 to 64 characters, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` | Name of the MASTER_ECU_KEY in the key store of the workstation (`%LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/csec/<name>.key` or `NX_CSEC_KEY_DIR`; create it with `nxconfig csec-key new`). A name, never the key: a value that looks like key material is refused. Left out: the board name. |
| `security.keys` | map of string to [object](#f-security-keys-key) |  | no | `{}` | key: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Flags per key; key: SHE name (`MASTER_ECU_KEY`, `BOOT_MAC_KEY`, `BOOT_MAC`, `KEY_1` ... `KEY_<n>` up to the free slots of `nvm.partition.key_slots`). A key left out gets no flags. |

<a id="f-security-keys-key"></a>

### `security.keys.<key>`

Attributes of one key of the security module (SHE key flags; s32k1xx: CSEc). Only what the key may be used for - the key value is never part of the project.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `security.keys.<key>.flags` | list of string |  | no | `[]` | item: `boot_protection`, `debugger_protection`, `key_usage`, `wildcard`, `verify_only` | SHE key flags set when the key is loaded: `boot_protection` (unusable after a failed secure boot), `debugger_protection` (unusable while a debugger is attached), `key_usage` (CMAC instead of encryption), `wildcard` (may be loaded without the chip UID), `verify_only` (CMAC verification only; needs `nvm.partition.key_verify_only`). WRITE_PROTECTION is deliberately not offered and refused in every spelling (NVM-14): one write-protected key makes the debug authentication - the only way back after a partition with key space - impossible for ever. |

<a id="f-bootloader"></a>

### `bootloader`

CAN bus and devices of the bootloader.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bootloader.can` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Board CAN bus of bootloader and updater; its bit timing is `can.<bus>`. |
| `bootloader.init` | list of string |  | no | `null` | item: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Board devices the bootloader switches on before CAN (drivers in `bootloader/devices/<module>`). Left out: the transceiver of `can`, if its module has a bootloader hook. Other used devices with a hook are only read (e.g. SBC watchdog). |
| `bootloader.sbc_watchdog` | string |  | no | `"leave"` | `leave`, `serve` | Watchdog of a system basis chip the bootloader switches on (`init`). `serve`: the bootloader sets the watchdog to the fixed period of the device hook (sbcUja113x: autonomous, 1024 ms) in Standby, enters Normal mode and triggers it while it runs; after the jump the application must take the watchdog over within that period (assumption of use). `leave`: takes effect only while the SBC is in software development mode (UJA113x: SDMS 1) - the bootloader does not touch the watchdog and enters Normal mode. Without development mode (SDMS 0) the watchdog runs from the SBC reset on, in Standby too (UJA113x: timeout, 128 ms), so the bootloader serves it as with `serve` whatever this value says (BL-41); the application takes it over the same way. This holds for an SBC that is only read (not in `init`) as well: with SDMS 0 the bootloader sets up and triggers only the watchdog, the SBC stays in Standby and V2 and CAN are not switched on (BL-42). `serve` differs from `leave` only with development mode: it also sets a watchdog the application left running to the fixed setting. The MTPNV is never changed. Boards without such an SBC: `leave`. |

<a id="f-diagnostics"></a>

### `diagnostics`

Diagnostic addresses of the ECU (doc/architecture/README.md, section 4: CAN ids and UDS addresses are a decision of the project). Used by the bootloader (bootloader/src/core), the application UDS stack (ecu/uds) and tools/canflash; generated into &lt;build>/generated/board/bootloader/bl_diag.h.

The CAN bus the application answers on is the diagnostic bus of the ECU description (rte.yaml uds.bus); the bootloader listens on bootloader.can.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics.request_id` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | CAN identifier of the physically addressed request (11 bit, must not collide with other identifiers of the bus). |
| `diagnostics.response_id` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | CAN identifier of the responses of this ECU. |
| `diagnostics.functional_id` | integer | none | no | `2015` | ≥ 0 | CAN identifier of the functionally addressed request (ISO 14229 "all nodes"). |
| `diagnostics.tester_address` | integer | none | no | `241` | 0 to 255 | Transport address of the tester (1 byte) in the UDS stack. |
| `diagnostics.ecu_address` | integer | none | no | `42` | 0 to 255 | Transport address of this ECU (1 byte) in the UDS stack. |
| `diagnostics.isotp` | [object](#f-diagnostics-isotp) |  | no | `{}` |  | ISO-TP parameters of the diagnostic connection. |
| `diagnostics.bootloader` | [object](#f-diagnostics-bootloader) |  | no | `{}` |  | Identification and security access of the bootloader. |

<a id="f-diagnostics-isotp"></a>

### `diagnostics.isotp`

ISO 15765-2 parameters of the diagnostic connection (normal addressing, classic CAN).

Bootloader and application answer with the same values, so one tester serves both. Ranges are the ones the protocol can encode; what is plausible for a download is checked in diag.py.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics.isotp.padding` | integer | none | no | `204` | 0 to 255 | Filler byte of frames shorter than 8 bytes. |
| `diagnostics.isotp.block_size` | integer | none | no | `0` | 0 to 255 | Block size BS of the flow control frame: consecutive frames before the next flow control; 0: no further flow control. |
| `diagnostics.isotp.stmin_ms` | integer | ms | no | `0` | 0 to 255 | Minimum separation time STmin of the flow control frame; at most 127. |
| `diagnostics.isotp.n_cr_ms` | integer | ms | no | `1000` | > 0 | Timeout N_Cr for the next consecutive frame. |
| `diagnostics.isotp.n_bs_ms` | integer | ms | no | `1000` | > 0 | Timeout N_Bs for the flow control frame. |

<a id="f-diagnostics-bootloader"></a>

### `diagnostics.bootloader`

How the bootloader identifies itself in its flash (DID 0xF180) and where the application looks for it.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics.bootloader.version_prefix` | string |  | no | `"nextbsw-bl"` | 1 to 24 characters, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$` | Prefix of the bootloader version string, without the version number: identifies the bootloader software. The application searches the bootloader area for it, the updater accepts an image with the same prefix and major version. The former name of the software (`S32K14x-BL`) is accepted as well, so boards flashed before the rename keep working. Compared byte by byte and case-sensitively. |
| `diagnostics.bootloader.scan_start` | integer | none | no | `null` | ≥ 0 | First address the application searches for the version string; the end is the start of the application. Left out: behind the flash area the family reserves (s32k1xx: vector table and flash configuration field up to 0x40F). |
| `diagnostics.bootloader.security` | [object](#f-diagnostics-bootloader-security) |  | no | `{}` |  | Security access of the bootloader (seed and key). |

<a id="f-diagnostics-bootloader-security"></a>

### `diagnostics.bootloader.security`

Security access of the bootloader. The device answers a seed with HMAC-SHA256(device key, seed); the device key is HMAC-SHA256(master key, chip UID) and is written once per device by the provisioning tool (tools/canflash/provision.py). The master key never enters the repository or the bootloader image: the project names it, the workstation holds it (%LOCALAPPDATA%/neXtBSW/keys/&lt;key>.key or an environment variable).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics.bootloader.security.method` | string |  | no | `"hmac-sha256"` | `hmac-sha256` | Method of the key calculation. |
| `diagnostics.bootloader.security.key` | string |  | no | `null` | 1 to 64 characters, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` | Name of the master key in the key store of the workstation. Left out: the board name - one key for every project of a board, so that switching between two applications of the same hardware keeps the provisioned device key. |
| `diagnostics.bootloader.security.allow_insecure_test_key` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the deliberately insecure test key of the repository (`nextbsw-insecure-test`) may be named in `key`. Test profiles only. |

<a id="f-xcp"></a>

### `xcp`

XCP on CAN: bus and CAN identifiers, a decision of the project like the diagnostic addresses. tools/rtegen generates xcp/xcpCanConfiguration.h from it (ecu/xcp, tools/a2lgen) and adds master_id to the hardware receive filter of the bus. diag.py checks range, bus and collisions with the YAML path (11/29 bit, diagnostics, DBC of the bus).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xcp.bus` | string |  | no | `null` | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Board CAN bus from `use.can` XCP runs on. Left out: the diagnostic bus. |
| `xcp.master_id` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 4294967295 | CAN identifier master -> ECU (commands, CTO); bit 31 set: 29-bit identifier (encoding of the DBC). |
| `xcp.slave_id` | integer | none | yes |  | 0 to 4294967295 | CAN identifier ECU -> master (responses and errors), same encoding as `master_id`. |

| `use.uart` | string or list of string |  | no | `[]` | `all`; item: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Used UARTs (`uart[].name` of the board): `all`, or a list of names from the board section of the same name. Left out: none. |

<a id="f-peripheral_clocks-key"></a>

### `peripheral_clocks.<key>`

The functional clock the project chooses for one peripheral instance.

`select` must be one of the sources the derivative allows (instances.&lt;x>.clock.sources), `divider` one of its asynchronous outputs - it may be left out when the derivative allows only one. Without an entry the default of the derivative applies, so a project that decides nothing keeps the values it had.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peripheral_clocks.<key>.select` | string |  | yes |  | `SOSC`, `SIRC`, `FIRC`, `SPLL` | Clock source that feeds the instance (s32k1xx: SOSC, SIRC, FIRC or SPLL, the value of PCCn.PCS). |
| `peripheral_clocks.<key>.divider` | integer |  | no | `null` | `1`, `2` | Asynchronous output of the source the clock is taken from: 1 for DIV1, 2 for DIV2. In a project entry it may be left out when the derivative allows only one output. |
| `peripheral_clocks.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the choice is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on a board). |
| `peripheral_clocks.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-can-key"></a>

### `can.<key>`

Bit timing request of a used board CAN bus; prescaler and segments are calculated (clock.py).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `can.<key>.bitrate` | integer | bit/s | yes |  | > 0 | Nominal bit rate of the bus (e.g. 500000). |
| `can.<key>.sample_point_percent` | number | % | no | `87.5` | 50 to 95, finite | Wanted sample point as a share of the bit time. The calculated bit timing may deviate slightly; nxconfig warns or reports an error when it deviates too far. |
| `can.<key>.sjw_tq` | integer | time quanta | no | `null` | > 0 | Synchronization jump width. Left out: as large as the segments allow. |
| `can.<key>.prop_seg_tq` | integer | time quanta | no | `null` | > 0 | Propagation segment. Left out: chosen so that phase segment 1 equals phase segment 2 where possible. |
| `can.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the bit timing is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on the bus). |
| `can.<key>.bus_off` | [object](#f-can-key-bus_off) |  | no | `null` |  | Behaviour of the bus after bus off (pause, dropping pending frames, logging). Left out: the defaults of every value. |

<a id="f-can-key-bus_off"></a>

### `can.<key>.bus_off`

What the bus does when a bus off keeps coming back: log series, doubling pause, dropping pending frames.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `can.<key>.bus_off.first_pause_ms` | integer | ms | no | `10` | 0 to 65535 | Pause before the first release of a series of bus offs: the controller stays in bus off this long before it is let back onto the bus. Default: one supervision cycle (10 ms). |
| `can.<key>.bus_off.max_pause_ms` | integer | ms | no | `1000` | 0 to 65535 | Upper limit of the pause, which doubles with every bus off of a series. `0`: the controller is not held and leaves bus off by itself (automatic recovery, as before COM-35); logging and dropping stay. |
| `can.<key>.bus_off.discard_after` | integer | none | no | `3` | 0 to 255 | From this bus off of a series on, the frames waiting in the transmit buffers are dropped before the release (a frame that already cost this many bus offs will cost the next one as well). `0`: never. |
| `can.<key>.bus_off.quiet_ms` | integer | ms | no | `2000` | 1 to 65535 | A series ends after this long without bus off; its end is logged in one line. Should be longer than `max_pause_ms`, so a lasting fault stays one series. |
| `can.<key>.bus_off.summary_ms` | integer | ms | no | `10000` | 1 to 65535 | While a series lasts, its further bus offs are counted and summarised in at most one line per this period. |
| `can.<key>.bus_off.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

| `i2c.<key>.timeout_ms` | integer | ms | no | `20` | 1 to 10000 | Time limit of one transfer, clock stretching of the device included; at least the longest transfer of the bus driver at the chosen rate. |

<a id="f-adc_loads-key-kind-ntc_beta"></a>

### `adc_loads.<key>` (kind: ntc_beta)

NTC after the beta model, R(T) = R_n * exp(B * (1/T - 1/T_n)); temperature in 0.1 degC.

The generator turns it into a table of points between t_min and t_max (step), the runtime interpolates.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adc_loads.<key>.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Data sheet or schematic the values come from. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: a value is not confirmed by the source. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.kind` | string |  | yes |  | `ntc_beta` | Load type: NTC thermistor described by the beta model; delivers the temperature in 0.1 °C. The board channel must deliver a resistance in ohm. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.r_nominal_ohm` | integer | Ω | yes |  | > 0, ≤ 2^31-1 | Resistance R_n at the nominal temperature. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.t_nominal_ddegc` | integer | 0.1 °C | no | `250` | -2731 to 10000 | Nominal temperature T_n (usually 25 °C). |
| `adc_loads.<key>.beta_k` | integer | K | yes |  | > 0, ≤ 100000 | Beta value B of the NTC, from its data sheet. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.t_min_ddegc` | integer | 0.1 °C | no | `-400` | -2731 to 10000 | Lowest temperature of the generated table. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.t_max_ddegc` | integer | 0.1 °C | no | `1500` | -2731 to 10000 | Highest temperature of the generated table. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.step_ddegc` | integer | 0.1 °C | no | `50` | > 0, ≤ 10000 | Temperature step between the points of the generated table. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.max_error_ddegc` | integer | 0.1 °C | no | `10` | > 0, ≤ 10000 | Largest interpolation error of the generated table that nxconfig accepts. |

<a id="f-adc_loads-key-kind-table"></a>

### `adc_loads.<key>` (kind: table)

Characteristic as points [board value, load value] with ascending board value; linear in between.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adc_loads.<key>.source` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Data sheet or schematic the values come from. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: a value is not confirmed by the source. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.kind` | string |  | yes |  | `table` | Load type: characteristic given as a table of points. |
| `adc_loads.<key>.unit` | string |  | yes |  | `mV`, `mA`, `ohm`, `ddegC`, `permille` | Unit of the load value (`adc.phys` of the channel). |
| `adc_loads.<key>.points` | list of list of integer | board unit, unit of `unit` | yes |  | 2 to 255 items; item: exactly 2 items; item: item: -2^31 to 2^31-1 | Points `[board value, load value]` with ascending board value, linear in between; the ends are held. The board value is in the unit the board channel delivers, the load value in `unit`. |

<a id="f-adc_sampling-key"></a>

### `adc_sampling.<key>`

Reading of a used board ADC channel other than one conversion per read.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adc_sampling.<key>.kind` | string |  | yes |  | `pwm_period_average` | Sampling of the channel: `pwm_period_average` converts `samples` times at equally spaced instants over exactly one realized period of `pwm_group` and delivers the rounded mean of the raw values. For channels that carry the ripple of a switching stage, e.g. the DC link current of a motor bridge; the conversion (`adc.phys`, `adc.mv`) applies to the mean. |
| `adc_sampling.<key>.pwm_group` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | PWM group of the project (`pwm.<group>`) whose realized period is averaged over. |
| `adc_sampling.<key>.samples` | integer | none | yes |  | 2 to 64 | Conversions per read, equally spaced over one period; they must fit into it (samples times the conversion time of `modules.bspAdcAccess`). Harmonics of the PWM frequency that are multiples of `samples` are not cancelled, so a sharper ripple needs more samples. The reading task is busy for one PWM period per read. |

<a id="f-interrupts-ranks-list"></a>

### `interrupts.ranks[]`

Rank of the interrupt of one board entry, e.g. {source: can, name: CAN0, rank: 3}.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |

| `interrupts.ranks[].source` | string |  | yes |  | `can`, `uart`, `spi`, `i2c`, `adc`, `input_capture`, `pwm`, `dio`, `sample_group` | Kind of board entry the interrupt belongs to. |
| `interrupts.ranks[].name` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Board entry of `source` (e.g. the CAN bus `CAN0`); the project must use it. |
| `interrupts.ranks[].rank` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Urgency rank; 0 is the most urgent interrupt that may call the RTOS. The hardware priority follows from the rank. |
| `interrupts.ranks[].note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-pin_events-key"></a>

### `pin_events.<key>`

Events on one digital input of the board (pin interrupt on an edge).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_events.<key>.edge` | string |  | yes |  | `activate`, `deactivate`, `both` | Edge that counts, relative to the active level of the board input (`dio.inputs[].active`): `activate` (the input becomes active), `deactivate` (it becomes inactive) or `both`. nxconfig derives the physical edge (rising/falling) from the board. |
| `pin_events.<key>.debounce_us` | integer | µs | yes |  | 0 to 1000000 | Software debounce: after an accepted edge, further edges are ignored for this time and the level is confirmed afterwards. 0: no debounce. Must be shorter than the shortest spacing the rate limit allows (`window_ms` / `max_events`). More than 0 needs edge detectors that report both edges (`pin_interrupts.edges` of the derivative). |
| `pin_events.<key>.max_events` | integer | none | yes |  | 1 to 65535 | Rate limit: at most this many candidate edges (edges of the configured direction, including the ones the debounce later drops as glitches) per `window_ms`. One more disarms the pin, the qualifier becomes QLF_ERROR (interrupt storm: bouncing contact, broken wire, fault on the line). |
| `pin_events.<key>.window_ms` | integer | ms | yes |  | 1 to 60000 | Time window of the rate limit. |
| `pin_events.<key>.rearm_ms` | integer | ms | yes |  | 1 to 600000 | Hold-off after the rate limit tripped: the pin is armed again automatically after this time. |
| `pin_events.<key>.wakeup` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | Reserved: the input as wake-up source of an MCU low-power mode. `true` is rejected until neXtBSW has an MCU low-power mode; today the ECU sleeps through the supply (SBC local wake inputs, `ecu.wakeup`). |
| `pin_events.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-safety"></a>

### `safety`

Pins of the OpenBSW safety demo.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `safety.safe_state_output` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Indicator of the safe state, a digital output: disabled (it floats) in the safe state and switched back with the level the application wrote last when the safe state is left. No actuator, and an output the application does not write - otherwise see `safe_state_output_shared_with_application`. |
| `safety.locked_pin` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Digital output whose pin configuration gets locked. |
| `safety.test_pin` | string |  | yes |  |  | Unconnected pin, checked cyclically as input. |
| `safety.safe_state_output_shared_with_application` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Confirms on purpose that the application writes `safe_state_output` (an rte.yaml `dio.out` target), with the reason as text - for example that the output is only a status LED. Entering the safe state disables the indicator's pin (it floats), leaving it switches the pin back with the level the application wrote last, so an actuator there would float in the safe state and come back on without an enable (AoU-30 of the safety concept). With the key, nxconfig does not warn about that case; without the case, the key itself is reported as superfluous. Left out: not confirmed. |
| `safety.output_groups` | list of [object](#f-safety-output_groups-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | **After R1.** Safe-output groups for the degraded reaction (SYS-117). Left out: none - every reaction switches all outputs, as before. |
| `safety.degraded` | list of [object](#f-safety-degraded-list) |  | no | `[]` |  | **After R1.** Events that report and switch only their safe-output groups instead of the fail-safe reaction (safe state for everything, reset). The rest of the ECU keeps running without a reset, the application reads the degraded groups from the RTE signal `safety.degraded`, and the groups stay degraded until the next power cycle, also across a reset. Left out: none - every event keeps its fail-safe reaction. |

<a id="f-safety-output_groups-list"></a>

### `safety.output_groups[]` (after R1)

After R1: part of the schema and checked by `tools/nxconfig`, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: `name`, `pwm`, `note`.

<a id="f-safety-degraded-list"></a>

### `safety.degraded[]` (after R1)

After R1: part of the schema and checked by `tools/nxconfig`, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: `event`, `device`, `groups`, `note`.

<a id="f-modules-key-key"></a>

### `modules.<key>.<key>`

Selective CAN wake-up (ISO 11898-2/-6 partial networking) of a system basis chip.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modules.<key>.<key>.id` | integer | none | yes |  | ≥ 0 | Identifier of the wake-up frame (11 or 29 bit). |
| `modules.<key>.<key>.extended` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: 29 bit identifier, `false`: 11 bit. |
| `modules.<key>.<key>.compare_mask` | integer | none | no | `null` | ≥ 0 | Identifier bits that must match (bit = 1); bits 0 are don't care. Left out: all bits, the frame must carry exactly `id`. |
| `modules.<key>.<key>.dlc` | integer | none | no | `null` | 0 to 8 | Data length the frame must have; with it the data field is part of the match. Left out: only the identifier is compared. |
| `modules.<key>.<key>.data_mask` | list of integer | none | no | `[]` | item: 0 to 255 | Per data byte 0..dlc-1: the frame wakes if one of its bits set here is set in the frame. Exactly `dlc` entries, at least one not 0 (left out with `dlc` 0). |
| `modules.<key>.<key>.fd_passive` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: CAN FD frames on the bus are tolerated in Sleep; `false`: they count as errors and wake the SBC after 32 of them. |

<a id="f-hw_thresholds-key"></a>

### `hw_thresholds.<key>` (after R1)

After R1: part of the schema and checked by `tools/nxconfig`, but not of the first release; the table is written when the object is. Keys: `input`, `trip`, `threshold`, `reference`, `pwm`, `filter_ns`, `verify`, `note`.

<a id="f-sample_groups-key"></a>

### `sample_groups.<key>`

Board ADC channels converted after every hardware trigger of a PWM group (fast control loop, IO-62).

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sample_groups.<key>.pwm` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | PWM group of the project (`pwm.<group>`) whose trigger output starts the group; the group needs `pwm.<group>.trigger`. |
| `sample_groups.<key>.channels` | list of string | none | yes |  | 1 to 32 items; item: at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Board ADC entries (`adc[].name`) of the group, in the order of the results. Entries on different ADCs are sampled at the same instant, entries on one ADC one after another in this order (nxconfig warns and names the time offset). |
| `sample_groups.<key>.delay_ns` | integer | ns | no | `0` | 0 to 1000000 | Time from the trigger point of the PWM group to the start of the first sample. The realised value is a whole number of sequencer clocks (nxconfig shows it). |
| `sample_groups.<key>.verify` | boolean |  | no | `false` |  | `true`: the sampling instant is not confirmed (e.g. not measured on a board). |
| `sample_groups.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-bsw_tasks-key"></a>

### `bsw_tasks.<key>`

Stack of one BSW task, or the task it runs in instead of a task of its own.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.stack_bytes` | integer | byte | no | `null` | > 0 | Stack of the task. At least `min_stack_bytes` of ecu/configuration/taskStacks.yaml and a multiple of its `multiple_of` (8, the safety task 32: MPU region). Below the default nxconfig warns: confirm the value with the high-water mark (console `stats`) or tools/stackuse. Left out: the default of taskStacks.yaml. |
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.run_in` | string |  | no | `null` | at least 1 character, pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` | Merge the task into another BSW task: no FreeRTOS task and no stack of its own, its work runs in the named task at that task's priority (its stack has to hold both). Only the merges taskStacks.yaml lists for the task (`run_in`); never for or into the safety task. Left out: the task runs on its own. |
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence` | [object](#f-bsw_tasks-key-evidence) |  | no | `null` |  | Proof note of the stack (tools/stackuse or high-water mark at the board). Required for a stack below the default in an ASIL project (project.integrity not `qm`), otherwise a warning. Left out: no proof noted. |
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |

<a id="f-bsw_tasks-key-evidence"></a>

### `bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence`

Proof note of a BSW task stack: what the task uses of its stack and where that is shown.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.method` | string |  | yes |  | `stackuse`, `high_water_mark` | Same as [`memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.method`](#f-memory-application-isr_stack_evidence). |
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.used_bytes` | integer | byte | yes |  | > 0 | Same as [`memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.used_bytes`](#f-memory-application-isr_stack_evidence). |
| `bsw_tasks.<key>.evidence.reference` | string |  | yes |  | at least 1 character | Same as [`memory.application.isr_stack_evidence.reference`](#f-memory-application-isr_stack_evidence). |

<a id="f-console"></a>

### `console`

Console and logger of the application on the terminal UART.

| Field | Type | Unit | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `console.enabled` | boolean |  | no | `true` |  | `false`: no console (no command input, no console commands of the application) and no logger (log calls do nothing, no ring buffer). The UART stays initialised: the safety lines of the safe supervisor (SAFETY RESET, safety::safeConsoleWrite) and the start-up lines are written to it synchronously in every image. Left out: `true`. |
| `console.logger_buffer_bytes` | integer | byte | no | `null` | 512 to 65536 | Size of the logger ring buffer. A full buffer drops the oldest entries (console `logger lost` counts them); below 8192 bytes the start-up of the eval board lost lines (board 2026-09-18). Left out: 8192. |
| `console.note` | string |  | no | `null` |  | Free text for the reader; no tool evaluates it. |
